title: The nature of sub-millimetre galaxies I: a comparison of AGN and star-forming galaxy SED fits
question: How well can a complete sample of 12 sub-millimetre galaxies in the William Herschel Deep Field be fitted with dust-obscured AGN template SEDs compared to similarly absorbed star-forming galaxy templates?

what.value: Original 870 um LABOCA catalogue, error circle radii, and optical/X-ray quasar identifications

evidence.quote: The observations were fully described by (cite: Bielby12) who compared eleven detected sub-mm sources in a central $16'$ diameter area of the WHDF to the Chandra X-ray sources, mainly identified as quasars (cite: mvm04).
For these we take the error circle radii, $\Delta\theta$, listed individually in Table 1 of (cite: Bielby12).

what.value: Chandra 75 ksec X-ray observations and initial source catalogue

evidence.quote: These data and their reduction and analysis were presented by (cite: mvm04) and an initial comparison to the WHDF LABOCA sources was carried out by (cite: Bielby12).

what.value: WHDF optical and NIR UBRIZHK photometry

evidence.quote: The William Herschel Deep Field (WHDF) is a $7'\times7'$ sky area (extended to $16'\times16'$) at RA(J2000)=00h22m33.3s, Dec=+00d20m57s, initially observed in the optical at the William Herschel 4.2-m telescope (cite: NM01) and in the NIR at the Calar Alto 3.5-m telescope (cite: NM06) to provide UBRIZHK photometry to $B\approx28$.

what.value: HST ACS i-band imaging of the WHDF

evidence.quote: Subsequently, it was observed with deep Chandra X-ray data, Hubble Space Telescope (HST) i-band imaging (cite: Bohm07; Ziegler09),

what.value: Spitzer IRAC Equatorial Survey (SPIES) 3.6 and 4.5 um catalogues

evidence.quote: Spitzer 3.6 and 4.5 $\mu$m data from the Spitzer IRAC Equatorial Survey (SPIES (cite: Timlin16)) cover $\approx115$ deg$^2$ of SDSS Stripe 82 and therefore contains the whole WHDF within this equatorial region.

what.value: Herschel HeLMS survey 250, 350, and 500 um catalogues

evidence.quote: The Herschel HeLMS survey (cite: Asboth16; Oliver12), covers the WHDF within its full 302 deg$^2$ area.

what.value: VLA 8.4 GHz radio observations and source fluxes

evidence.quote: VLA data for the central $7'\times7'$ at 8.4 GHz (3.57cm) were reported by (cite: Heywood13).

what.value: Median AS2UDS star-forming galaxy SED template

evidence.quote: Our other star-forming galaxy model was made by taking the median star-forming galaxy fit from the $\approx700$ sub-mm sources of (cite: Dud20) in the AS2UDS survey.

what.value: Average Milky Way dust reddening curve data (R_V = 3.1)

evidence.quote: The reddening law is a fit to the average Milky Way reddening curve data ($R_V=3.1$) taken from Fig. 10 of (cite: Gordon03), following (cite: Cardelli89) in the range $0.3<x<11.0$ where $x=1/\lambda$ with wavelength, $\lambda$, measured in microns.

recipe.goal: Reduce ALMA 870 um continuum images and measure source positions and fluxes
recipe.method: Reduce ALMA data with the CASA imaging pipeline and fit sources for ellipticity, flux, and position using IMFIT
key_parameters: 870 um continuum at 0.095 arcsec resolution, rms 65 uJy/beam

recipe.goal: Reanalyse Chandra X-ray data at ALMA and LABOCA positions
recipe.method: Measure X-ray photon fluxes in three energy bands (0.5-1.2, 1.2-2.0, and 2-7 keV) at ALMA and optical counterpart positions to formal S/N > 1.43 (90% confidence) using CIAO srcflux
key_parameters: Energy bands: 0.5-1.2, 1.2-2.0, and 2-7 keV; S/N > 1.43 (90% confidence)

recipe.goal: Astrometrically correct optical/NIR catalogues and cross-match multi-wavelength counterparts
recipe.method: Correct WHDF r and H band astrometry to the DECaLS frame and cross-match ALMA/LABOCA positions with WHDF optical/NIR, HST i, Spitzer SPIES, Herschel HeLMS, and VLA 8.4 GHz catalogues
key_parameters: WHDF-ALMA matching radius < 1.3 arcsec; HST-ALMA radius = 0.65 arcsec; HeLMS matching radii = 20, 30, 40 arcsec at 250, 350, 500 um
assumptions: Expected false optical counterpart contamination is ~0.12 sources per 1.3 arcsec circle at r = 26.3

recipe.goal: Construct empirical AGN and star-forming galaxy SED templates and dust reddening law
recipe.method: Fit analytic power-law and quadratic functions to unabsorbed WHDF X-ray QSO SEDs (1PL and 1.4 um Dip), LAB-06 (SF6), and median AS2UDS SMG SED (AS2), and apply a polynomial Milky Way dust reddening curve
key_parameters: 4 templates: 1PL AGN, 1.4 um Dip AGN, SF6 (LAB-06 spiral), AS2UDS median SMG
assumptions: Fixed 25% flux transmission below 0.1216 um for Lyman-alpha forest absorption in AGN templates; Milky Way R_V = 3.1 reddening law extrapolated as 1/lambda for lambda > 3.33 um

recipe.goal: Fit optical-MIR and FIR-sub-mm SEDs to derive redshift, extinction, dust temperature, and dust mass
recipe.method: Perform maximum likelihood SED fitting (including upper limits) on a grid of z, A_V, and gray-body temperature T in Fortran, combining optical-NIR and FIR-sub-mm likelihoods and computing dust mass M_d
key_parameters: Grid ranges: 0 < z < 4.5 (step 0.1), 0 < A_V < 2.5 mag (step 0.25 mag), 10 < T < 50 K (step 1 K); 5 fitted parameters (z, A_V, T, S_Opt/IR, S_FIR) with Delta chi^2 = 5.89 for 1-sigma errors
assumptions: Dust mass opacity coefficient kappa = 0.077 * (nu / 352.0e9)^beta m^2 kg^-1 with emissivity index beta = 1.8; Cosmology: Omega_lambda = 0.7, Omega_m = 0.3, H_0 = 100 km s^-1 Mpc^-1; HeLMS upper limits = 20 mJy; SPIES upper limits = 2 uJy

evidence.loc: WHDF Flux Errors, Coordinates and Magnitudes

answer_key.quantity: Average AGN fitted redshift (11 SMGs excluding LAB-06)

evidence.quote: The 11 AGN redshifts (excluding the star-forming galaxy LAB-06) range from $0<z<4.5$ with an average $z=2.43\pm0.31$ and the absorptions range from $0<A_V<2.5$ mag with an average of $A_V=1.25\pm0.25$ mag.

answer_key.quantity: Average AGN fitted visual absorption A_V (11 SMGs excluding LAB-06)

evidence.quote: The 11 AGN redshifts (excluding the star-forming galaxy LAB-06) range from $0<z<4.5$ with an average $z=2.43\pm0.31$ and the absorptions range from $0<A_V<2.5$ mag with an average of $A_V=1.25\pm0.25$ mag.

answer_key.quantity: Average AGN fitted dust mass M_d (7 SMGs with >1 FIR point, excluding LAB-06)

evidence.quote: For the AGN FIR fits that have more than one FIR data point and again excluding LAB-06 we find that the dust mass ranges between $1.1<M_d<4.9\times10^8M_\odot$ with an average of $M_d=1.77\pm0.46\times10^8M_\odot$.

answer_key.quantity: Average AGN fitted dust temperature T (7 SMGs with >1 FIR point, excluding LAB-06)

evidence.quote: The dust temperatures for these 7 (including the LAB-08 lower limit of 50K) range from $21<T<50$K with an average $T=39.3\pm3.6$K.

answer_key.quantity: Fraction of SMGs fitted at least as well by AGN as SFG templates

evidence.quote: We conclude that AGN make at least as good fits to 10/12 or $83\pm26$% of sub-mm sources with only 1 source ($\approx8$%) where a star-forming galaxy was clearly the better fit, the $z=0.046$ spiral galaxy, LAB-06.

answer_key.quantity: Minimum AGN fraction among the 8 SMGs with ALMA positions (X-ray detected)

evidence.quote: We again emphasise that the minimum AGN fraction of the 8 with ALMA positions comprises those with X-ray detections i.e. LAB-01, LAB-03, LAB-04, LAB-05, LAB-11 ie 5/8 or 62.5%.

answer_key.quantity: LAB-01 AGN best-fit redshift, A_V, T, and M_d
answer_key.units: z: dimensionless, A_V: mag, T: K, M_d: M_sun

score_reason: The complete multi-wavelength flux and error tables (Tables 1 and A1), source coordinates (Tables A2-A4), analytic SED template equations (Eqs. 1-8), dust reddening polynomials (Eqs. 9-11), and grid parameters are all explicitly provided in the text, making the SED fitting highly reproducible from the published tables, though the custom Fortran code, template normalizations, and detailed ALMA imaging settings (deferred to Paper II) are omitted.
rediscovery_reason: The ALMA dataset (2016.1.01523.S) is public in the ALMA archive, the complete multi-wavelength flux and error tables are printed in full in the paper, and the main results (ALMA counterpart coordinates, redshifts, A_V, dust temperatures, dust masses, and delta-chi^2 values) are concrete numeric targets.
